Jack Parr was a professional basketball player.
Jack Parr was born in Louisville, Kentucky.
Jack Parr played college basketball at Kansas State University.
Jack Parr's jersey (number 33) was retired by Kansas State.
Jack Parr was drafted by the Cincinnati Royals in the 10th round of the 1958 NBA draft.
Jack Parr played 66 games for the Cincinnati Royals in 1958–1959, averaging 4.0 points per game.
Jack Parr was not a picture player early in his career.
Jack Parr had intensity and inner drive.
Jack Parr's shots included a hook and a soft "face the basket" jumper.
Jack Parr made a defensive play against Kansas in Lawrence in 1958.
Jack Parr gained all-league honors three times.
Jack Parr helped the Wildcats to conference championships and NCAA play twice.
Jack Parr received All-America recognition twice.
Jack Parr holds KSU's single-season rebounding record.
Jack Parr is second on the career charts.
Jack Parr ranks 10th among the all-time Wildcat scoring leaders with 1,184 points.
Jack Parr played one season professionally with the Cincinnati Royals before turning to private business and becoming a Big Eight basketball official.
Jack Parr died in January 2015, aged 78, at his home in Lindsborg, Kansas.
